title: Attention-pathway latency signature profiling and adaptive kernel switch telemetry
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Current runtime telemetry captures per-kernel timings and NVTX ranges, but we lack a compact, request-level "latency signature" that ties attention pathway choices, kernel variant selection, and prefill/decode scheduling decisions to end-to-end latency and tail behavior. This makes it hard to: 1) detect regressions caused by attention fallback heuristics, 2) audit why a particular request took a slow kernel path, and 3) produce compact dashboards for SLA/pg queries.

Goal: Produce an instrumentation and profiling design that emits a lightweight per-request latency signature and enrichment fields that: 1) correlate chosen attention pathway (e.g., fused-attn-vs-slower-unfused, sparse vs dense fallback), 2) record kernel variant id and quantization profile used, 3) capture prefill/decode scheduler decisions (delayed batching, priority demotion), and 4) expose NVTX range ids and span linkage suitable for trace visualization and aggregation.

Success metrics:
- 90% of requests have a complete latency signature in traces for a sampled 1:1000 traffic slice.
- Signal enables root-cause analysis for >80% of high-p90 latency incidents in the next quarter.
- Additional telemetry volume increase <8% at 1:1000 sampling.

Approach:
1) Design a compact latency_signature payload that is attached as trace/span tags and as a sparse log entry for downstream batching analysis. Fields: attention_pathway (string), kernel_variant (string), kernel_exec_hash (string), quant_profile (string), prefill_scheduler_decision (string), decode_scheduler_decision (string), token_range_ms (string), nvtx_ranges (comma-separated ids).
2) Instrument attention router to emit an enum attention_pathway at decision time and attach NVTX id boundaries to the prefill and decode NVTX groups.
3) Add a kernel_exec_hash generated from (kernel_name, kernel_args_signature, cu_id, launch_config) to correlate with GPU profiler dumps.
4) Extend tracer span schema with latency_signature tag and a short binary-safe base64 payload for heavy cases (falls back to tag set when tracer size constrained).
5) Sampling: enable a micro-sampler that captures full latency_signature for 0.1% of requests and only header tags for another 1% for aggregation.
6) Backfill dashboards: a new "latency-signatures" rollup in Console to show distribution by attention_pathway and kernel_variant.

Instrumentation plan:
- Prefill path: emit NVTX range start/end with a unique trace-local id; attach attention_pathway when the router picks a path (fused, block-sparse, matmul-slow-fallback).
- Decode path: record scheduler decisions (immediate, batched-delay-ms, preempted) and link to the same trace id to assemble the signature during trace ingestion.
- Kernel metrics: capture per-kernel launched thread/block/warp utilization counters (where available) and tag with kernel_exec_hash.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Adding kernel_exec_hash increases metadata size; mitigate by sampling and hashing to 16 hex chars.
- NVTX id explosion if we use trace-local sequential ids; instead use short randomized 8-char ids and keep mapping in span tags.
- Some low-latency code paths cannot afford heap allocations per-request; plan uses stack-allocated small buffers and preallocated tag slots for hot paths.

Rollout:
Phase 1 (canary): implement micro-sampler and signature tags for hosted runtime in us-west-2 on a small service fleet (2% traffic) — two weeks.
Phase 2 (broader): expand to 10% traffic and land Console dashboards + alerting for attention_pathway regressions — four weeks.
Phase 3: Dedicated & Private opt-in toggle with config flags and KMS-safe logging for enterprise compliance — six weeks.

Open questions:
- Do we want to fold quant_profile into kernel_variant or keep separate? (Engineering leaning: separate for easier cardinality control.)
- Where should long-lived kernel exec mapping be stored for offline profiler joins? Options: S3 blob per-day vs low-cardinality DB. (Prefer S3 blobs keyed by runtime-version+date.)

comments: 2026-03-03 — Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to 16-hex kernel_exec_hash and 8-char NVTX ids. Rishi to prototype router tagging. PM (Leah Ortiz) asked for dashboard mockups.

2026-03-06 — Rishi Patel: Prototype in branch feat/attn-signature-proto. Prefill path instrumentation emits trace tag 'latency_signature_v1' with compact fields. Early canary shows +2.3% trace size at 0.1% sampling. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1198

2026-03-08 — Performance results: Microbench on rtx-a100 cluster shows no measurable p50 change; p95 increase on batched-prefill synthetic workload by ~1.8ms when full payload is attached on every request. Decided to enforce sampling to keep overhead low.

2026-03-10 — Design review: UX feedback from Console team (Marta Lopez): need a rollup that groups by attention_pathway and kernel_variant with an 'incident explorer' that filters by latency_signature fields. Added to scope as Console ticket PM-6821.

2026-03-12 — Blocker: observed mismatch between kernel_exec_hash generated in runtime and execution fingerprint in nvprof dumps due to launch_config normalization differences. Action: add canonicalizer function and test vectors. Assigned to SRE: Jon Park.

2026-03-13 — Rishi Patel: Submitted updated PR with sampling configuration knobs and stack-alloc buffer pool to avoid allocations on hot path. Requesting code review from eng leads (tagged: @MayaSingh, @EthanG).
